claims.text: Thermal exposure drives the microstructural evolution of the metastable Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy.
The microstructural evolution proceeds through nucleation of Mg-rich intermetallic compounds.
The microstructural evolution proceeds through growth of Mg-rich intermetallic compounds.
Formation of Mg-rich intermetallic compounds reduces corrosion resistance.
Formation of Mg-rich intermetallic compounds reduces high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Thermal activation promotes diffusion of Mg atoms.
Mg diffusion leads to the formation of Mg-rich intermetallic compounds.
Formation of Mg-rich intermetallic compounds depletes Mg from the matrix.
Depletion of Mg from the matrix reduces the alloy's ability to form protective oxide layers.
Reduced formation of protective oxide layers diminishes oxidation resistance.
The newly formed intermetallic phases are less protective than the initial metastable matrix.
The initial metastable solid-solution state has relatively high corrosion resistance because Mg is present in the matrix.
The initial metastable solid-solution state has relatively high oxidation resistance because Mg is present in the matrix.
After thermal exposure, Mg content in the matrix will decrease relative to the initial state.
After thermal exposure, corrosion resistance will measurably decrease relative to the initial metastable state.
After thermal exposure, high-temperature oxidation resistance will measurably decrease relative to the initial metastable state.
The proposed transformation and degradation pathway applies under atmospheric exposure between approximately 300°C and 600°C.

contradictions.description: The conditions include temperatures ranging from 300°C to 600°C, whereas the boundary specifies temperatures strictly above 300°C and below 600°C, leaving the endpoint inclusion inconsistent.
